lesson.grammar_point: should / shouldn't for advice and recommendations

listenings.text: Hi Rodrigo, it's Claire. I read your report about the stockout. My advice: you shouldn't use the second supplier every month, because it is expensive. You should talk to the customer about the forecast for next year. And you should send me the numbers on Friday. We can talk on Monday. Thank you!

New York in October: three tips for visitors. First, the weather is cool, so you should bring a jacket. Second, you should use the subway: it is fast and it is cheap. And you shouldn't take a taxi at five in the afternoon, because the traffic is terrible. Enjoy the city!

extra_audio.text: A big customer called with an urgent order. The demand was high, but the forecast was low. Rodrigo asked Claire for advice. She said: you should call the customer today. Now the team updates the forecast every week.

reading.rtitle: Case Study -- A Stockout at the Plant
paras: Last month, a big customer in São Paulo asked for three times the normal amount of a strawberry flavor. The forecast was wrong, so the plant did not have enough raw material.
The problem. The demand was very high and the stock was low. Two orders were late, and the customer was not happy.
The options. The team can buy raw material from a second supplier, but it is more expensive. Or the plant can work on Saturday, but the team is tired.

The advice of the global team. "You should call the customer today and explain the situation. You shouldn't promise a date that you cannot keep. And you should update the forecast every week, not every month."
The decision. The priority is the customer. This month, the plant is going to buy from the second supplier.
